title: DON'T Play RuneScape Dragonwilds 1.0.1 Until You Know THIS!
author: BiggySweats
chapters: Dragonwilds 1.0.1 — What You Need to Know
Your Equipment Has Changed — Ring Slots & Glory Nerf
Death From Above — How It Works
Raid Skips, Kuldra & Ascension Core Fixes
description:
RuneScape Dragonwilds 1.0.1 has changed quite a few things, and if you're jumping back into the game, some of your old equipment choices and combat setups might need another look.

This update brings new Ranged special attacks, separate Ring and Amulet slots, an Amulet of Glory nerf, stronger Rune ammunition, Death From Above, 8 extra inventory slots, improved quest tracking, enemy aggression changes, farming upgrades, raid fixes and important save recovery improvements.

If you've been playing Dragonwilds since 1.0, these are the biggest changes worth knowing before you jump back in, including what I'd check first, which upgrades actually matter and some reported issues to watch out for.

transcript.text: Runescape Dragonfire's just got its 1.0.1 update and if you're jumping back into the game, there's actually quite a
few things you need to know. And I'm not just talking about a few extra inventory slots or fixing some bugs. You can now
equip a ring and an amulet at the same time, which is brilliant. Except the amulet of glory has also been nerfed. So
some of the equipment choices you were making yesterday aren't quite the same anymore considering we just made a video
on it. Range combat has also got three completely different special attacks. Rune ammunition has been buffed and
there's a new skill that lets you slow enemies down by shooting them in the legs. But there is also some smaller
changes that affect how you explore, farm resources and even get through the raid. So let's go through what actually
matters in 1.0.1, what I'd be checking first and a couple of problems you should probably know about before
jumping back in. Right, first up, jewelry because it's probably one of my favorite changes in the entire update.
We finally got separate equipment slots for rings and amulets. Previously, if you wanted to wear something like the
ring of life, you had to give up whatever amulet you were using, which was quite annoying, especially if you
spent ages grinding something like the amulet of glory. Well, not anymore. You can now have your amulet equipped for
the normal bonuses and use a ring alongside it. So if you've been keeping useful rings in your storage because you
didn't want to sacrifice your damage, go and have another look at them. But here's the catch. Jagex has also nerfed
the amulet of glory. Apparently, it was providing stronger bonuses than they originally intended, so those have now
been reduced. And that's quite important because glory was one of the strongest general purpose jewelry options before
this patch. certainly mean the amulet is rubbish. It's still useful across multiple combat styles. But if you're
using older gear guides, including my own, don't assume those previous damage numbers are still correct. I'd be
checking whether glory is still the right choice for what you're actually fighting rather than just equipping it
because it used to be an obvious upgrade. And I wouldn't go and replace it with an unholy symbol without
considering the health penalty, either. More damage is lovely, but not if you're getting your head kicked in every 30
seconds. Now, this is probably the biggest actual gameplay change. Range weapons have finally got their own
special attacks and what's interesting is that Jagex hasn't just given every bow the same ability. Short bows now
have rapid fire. Your character jumps backwards and fires three arrows in quick succession and you can actually
switch targets during the attack. So, rather than standing there firing at one enemy while three of us run towards you,
you've now got another way to attack while creating some distance. Long bows get power shot. You take the knee, draw
a bow and fire a much more powerful shot over a longer distance. That's the one I'd be looking at when you're opening a
fight and you've got time to line up your target properly. Then, crossbows get heavy ball. You charge up a stronger
shot, but the interesting bit here is that it also applies enchanted ammunition effects when it's hit. And
that makes enchanted bolts worth another look because your special attack now has more going on than simply hitting
something harder. But, before everybody goes and bins their current weapon, this doesn't automatically mean we've got a
completely new best crossbow. Damage, speed, ammunition cost and special effects still matter massively. I want
to see proper comparisons before telling people to spend hours upgrading something that might not actually be
better for their build. And there's another range change that could make a massive difference. Rune arrows and
bolts have been buffed. Jagex has increased their damage multiplier to 4.9 compared with 4.2 for adamant. So, if
you've been carrying on using adamant ammunition because it was doing the job perfectly fine before, rune is now worth
considering when you want the extra damage. Obviously, you've still got the ammunition, so I'm not telling you to
waste your entire supply shooting every random goblin you walk past. There's also a new perk called low blow and I
actually really like the idea behind this one. If you hit an enemy in the legs or roughly the lower third of his
body, you can apply a debuff called hamstring that temporarily slows its movement speed. So, if you're playing
range and constantly having enemies running straight into your face, this gives you another way to keep your
distance. It doesn't work on tiny or colossal enemies though, so don't expect to shoot some enormous boss in the ankle
and suddenly turn it into a snail. Then you've got armor recovery and greater armor recovery further along the range
skill tree. These give you chances to recover arrows from enemies you've killed and considering how much
ammunition you get through when you're properly using range, that's a pretty welcome addition. Between these perks,
the special attacks and the ammunition changes, range has a lot more going for it than it did before. Whether it's now
the strongest combat style is a different question. But if you've been ignoring range for most of your play
through, I'd definitely give it another look. And then there's death from above. This is the new jump attack and one
thing worth knowing is that it doesn't work just because you press jump. You actually need to unlock the death from
above perk first and then you need to get high enough above the ground before attacking. Jagex specifically says you
need to be slightly higher than the maximum height of a double jump. So if you've unlocked the skill, you're
jumping around on flat ground and wondering why absolutely nothing is happening, well, that's probably why.
You can jump from somewhere higher or use wind step to get the height you need, then attack while you're up there
and you'll come crashing down whatever unfortunate thing is standing around you. The damage scales with your
equipped weapon, so it isn't just a fixed little bit of damage regardless on what you're carrying. I'm interested to
see how useful this becomes in normal combat, but at the very least we finally got another reason to launch ourselves
into the air. As if we needed one. Now this next change isn't nearly as flashy, but bloody hell was it needed. Your
inventory has gone from 32 slots to 40 slots. Eight extra just from updating the game. You don't need to craft a new
backpack or go hunting for some special upgrade. And if you've spent any significant amount of time farming
resources in Dragon Wilds, you know how quickly your inventory fills up. So eight more spaces for food, tools,
ammunition or whatever random materials you're refusing to throw away is brilliant. Just remember more inventory
slots doesn't mean your maximum carrying weight has increased. You can fit more items in your bag, but you can still end
up massively overweight. And if you've watched my previous video about lodestones, you'll know why that can get
expensive. Inventory sorting has also improved. You can now stack by total weight, item type, and whichever items
you've picked up recently. Then we've got some surprisingly nice quest changes. You can track a main quest, a
side quest, and a task at the same time. And the update interface gives you much better information about where you're
supposed to be going. I have said this from day zero of RuneScape Dragon Wilds, we needed something like this massively.
There is also a completed quest tab, which is handy if you've come back after a break and have absolutely no idea what
you've already done. And spells can now be quick cast directly from the spell wheel. That's especially nice for
something like wind step, where having to constantly fiddle around with your spells gets super annoying. If you're
playing on controller, though, some of these controls have changed. worth spending a minute getting used to the
new layout. And if these Dragon Wilds videos are helping you figure out what's actually worth your time, you can become
a channel member down below. It helps me keep making these guides, and I massively appreciate everyone who's
already supporting the channel. Never expected, always appreciated. And if you're new here, hit that subscribe
button and join the sweats because we've got plenty more games to come. So, exploring. Jagex has reduced enemy
aggression ranges, so you shouldn't have quite as many situations where you're trying to get somewhere and half of the
region decides to chase you through it. Enemies should also chase you for shorter distances, which is lovely when
you're just trying to explore without fighting absolutely everything. But, they've also increased enemy response
timers. So, once you've cleared an area, enemies are going to stay dead for longer. It's brilliant if you're
exploring, gathering resources, or trying to get through somewhere safely. Not necessarily brilliant if you've been
farming the same group of enemies over and over for specific drops because now you could be waiting longer for them to
come back. So, if one of your farming route suddenly feels slower after the update, this might be why. I'd be
looking at moving between different groups of enemies rather than standing around waiting for the same ones to
respawn. There's also some good news for farming back at your base. We've got a ultra compost bin and a larger compost
bucket. Plus, overdrive can now be used on the advanced spinning wheel. Nothing particularly complicated here, but if
you're doing a lot of farming or processing materials, these are worth checking out. Now, one for anybody
repeatedly running the scorched wilderness raid, Jagex has fixed several wind step related skips. They've also
fixed the issue where the or could respawn immediately when teleporting during the raid. So, if you've been
relying on either one of those to speed up your runs, don't just assume your old route still works exactly the same.
Notice I said several skips, not every single skip, because there's a difference between Jagex fixing some
unintended shortcuts and me telling you that absolutely everything has been patched. They've also fixed enemies and
obstacles not respawning correctly when starting another raid run. And there's a fix for situations where Kerapac wasn't
dropping ascension cores properly. The last one is worth knowing if you're working through weapon upgrades, but it
doesn't mean you're suddenly guaranteed an ascension core every time you kill Kerapac. It's a fix for cases where the
drops weren't working as intended. So, I'd still go into the fights with realistic expectations. So, we need to
talk about save issues because this is probably the most important part of the update for anybody who's actually been
affected. Jagex has introduced fixes targeting disappearing world saves. There's also a recovery system for
corrupted characters allowing affected players to return with reconstructed skill progress and tier four equipment.
But this is important. It doesn't mean every affected player is guaranteed to get their original character and every
item back exactly as they were. Jagex has said there may still be a small number of unresolved save problems that
they're investigating. So, if your world or character disappeared, previously absolutely check whether you can get
back in. Just don't assume every case has been solved. And there's something else worth knowing. Players have been
reporting that the fourth attack in the air magic staff combo isn't registering damage properly after the patch. That's
been reported across multiple different platforms. So, if you're using air magic and suddenly wondering why your final
attack isn't doing anything, you are not the only one. There is also a reported room crafting issue where selecting a
larger quantity of essence can reset it back to one. Some players have reported temporary workarounds, but I wouldn't
treat those as guaranteed fixes. These are reported problems, not intentional changes, and they may be addressed in
another patch. So, if you're experiencing them, keep an eye on official updates before changing your
entire build or assuming you've done something wrong. And before we finish, if you're grabbing any game or service,
remember you can use the code Biggy for 10% off at checkout through my link down below. Sadly, it won't fix your air
magic combo, but at least you guys will get a discount on something. But, I actually want to know something from you
guys. What's the biggest change you've noticed in 1.0.1, and have you found anything that Jagex hasn't mentioned in
the patch notes? Because between the new combat skills, equipment changes, and all the smaller fixes, I'm interested to
see what people discover once they've had more time with the update. So, chuck that in the comments. If this video
helped, hit like, subscribe, and join the sweats. I've got plenty more videos to come. Patreon, Twitch, and all my
socials are linked down below. Get following. I'll catch you in the next one, guys. Peace.
